evidence_scope: Host layout, serialization and rejection tests only; no native isolation, queue execution, DMA, firmware, GPU, transport or service compatibility is established.
encoding_rules: Encode and decode each explicit-width unsigned scalar in little-endian order; serialized descriptors contain no host pointers, implicit padding or language object layouts.

Native C/Rust structs describe layout, not a portable serialization procedure. Copying their memory is not a conforming encoder on big-endian hosts. Never dereference an untrusted byte buffer as a typed struct.

A decoder receives one exact frame and checks major=1, minor=0, known kind, exact declared size and actual size, all flags/reserved fields zero, known enums, and all width/bounds rules before any authority lookup or execution.

Top-level cross-domain descriptors have 8-byte layout alignment; embedded Header has natural alignment 4. A byte decoder accepts arbitrary input alignment and copies scalar bytes. Native mapping alignment is checked independently.

CapabilityRef all zeros denotes absent authority; a present reference requires nonzero generation and domain. Slot zero is valid. A serialized reference is untrusted until resolved in the authenticated receiving namespace.
No descriptor alone grants authority: capability rights, namespace, current generation, task/budget ownership, placement epoch, expiry and region capacity are checked against trusted service state.

Offset plus length must not overflow u64; bounds are checked with subtraction against the resolved region length. A buffer remains owned until outstanding references and device/transfer work are drained or reset.
Zero placement_epoch denotes local work without distributed placement authority; distributed services require their currently committed nonzero epoch.
No unknown operation/status/milestone is interpreted as success. An unsupported operation returns invalid_descriptor or a documented unsupported service outcome without performing work.

Negotiation: required_features and supported_features contain no unknown bits
required_features is a subset of supported_features
choose the highest common supported version or return unsupported_version; do not reinterpret a future descriptor
Submission: cancel/fence require absent region, zero offset and zero length
deadline_ns=0 means no deadline; other values use the owning node monotonic clock and are never compared across hosts
Completion: present region requires nonzero ownership_generation; its match to trusted outstanding work is a contextual check independent of capability-handle generation
absent region requires produced_length=0 and ownership_generation=0
produced_length must fit the resolved region
status=ok cannot certify fault_reported; fault_reported requires a non-ok status
status=ok with a cancellation milestone reports that milestone only, never whole-task completion

operation_semantics.copy: Authorized service copy described by service-specific validated metadata in the referenced region. This generic descriptor does not invent a source/destination address or grant raw DMA.
operation_semantics.execute: Submit a qualified prepared operation/graph whose service-specific metadata is in the referenced region; unsupported formats are rejected.
operation_semantics.transfer: Submit a bounded transfer with authenticated peer metadata in the referenced region. Protocol and backend selection are outside ABI v1.
operation_semantics.cancel: Request cancellation of task_id at placement_epoch; request_id identifies this control request. Acknowledgment cannot imply launch interruption, output fencing or memory reclamation.
operation_semantics.fence: Request fencing of task_id at placement_epoch. Acceptance requires existing authority; the command cannot assign a new committed epoch.
operation_semantics.release: Request release of the referenced region. It may complete only after lifetime checks and required drain/reset; the request never revokes another namespace without authority.

queue_boundary: These layouts do not yet choose K04 ring atomics, wraparound, sequence allocation, queue capacity, backpressure ordering, crash recovery, or DMA fences. Queue implementations require separate conformance evidence.

portable_records.encoding: Versioned UTF-8 JSON schema records, not packed kernel descriptors; no host pointers or implicit language layouts.
portable_records.profile: compatibility.json model_profile and the host manifest validator define the bounded fixture vocabulary and exact-match rejection rules.
records: shard index/count and half-open layer ownership
operator identifiers and supported operation vocabulary
state representation, ownership generation and placement epoch
portable_records.scope: Only an artificial conformance fixture is admitted; no production model architecture, executable backend or state conversion is qualified.
